scope: Tail-read latency on a described-cache miss, forwarding the spec head itself (direct, cache.prefix "checkpoint") vs starting after a held tail prefix that background prefill made (cache.prefix "tail"). benchmarks/lfm25/tail_prefill.py against one daemon built from chat-tail 4dc5588, spec demo/specs/email-triage-v2.json, --device rocm --threads 8 --adjudicator-context 4096, default budgets.
conditions: zorak gfx1151, under the zorak-heavy lock and a MemAvailable >= 8 GiB guard. Resident on the GPU during the run: the live lfm2d pod (mostly idle), a kaiseki torch process holding 68 GB, and another agent's lfm2d-tail daemon (idle as far as seen); MemAvailable ~31 GiB. Six scenario chats, two streamed turns each, n = 12 per class. Direct reads ran mid-turn at the checkpoint event (served at the generation's pauses); prefix reads after 3 s idle on the assistant checkpoint, whose chat carries the assistant turn, so they read longer prompts (p50 1215 vs 560 tokens). Background prefill of the 304-token head took 530-590 ms per checkpoint (daemon log).
